item.title: Proof, Not Promises
item.description:

item.title: Where the Bottleneck Moved
item.description:
Accuracy over parallelism: Nabil A on going from seven parallel coding agents back to one, AWS's six-control gated review pipeline with risk tiers, StarSling's A/B-tested self-improving CI, GitHub Event Streams and new agent safety and measurement tools, and Azure SRE Agent at Ignite. Practical idea: a deterministic risk-tier labeller for every agent PR.

Sources discussed:

  • We Ran Seven Coding Agents in Parallel. Then We Went Back to One. (Nabil A, DEV)
  • Building a gated review pipeline for AI coding agents on AWS (AWS DevOps Blog)
  • Launch HN: StarSling (YC P25) – Self-improving CI for agent-volume repos
  • StarSling (vendor site)
  • StarSling open skills on GitHub
  • GitHub Event Streams is now in preview (GitHub Changelog)
  • Secret scanning on demand for developers and agents (GitHub Changelog)
  • GitHub Copilot Evals is now in public preview (GitHub Changelog)
  • Track Copilot code review outcomes in Repository insights (GitHub Changelog)
  • What's new in Azure SRE Agent at Microsoft Ignite 2026 (Microsoft Tech Community)
  • GitHub Copilot app: Microsoft Ignite releases (GitHub Changelog)
  • You let the agent merge its own PR. CI was green. That's the problem. (Powerduck blog)
  • Why we built Satoru, our background coding agent (Roboto Studio)

item.title: Green Is Not the Same as Proven

item.title: Software Factory News - Fri 13 Nov 2026
item.description:
Friday's theme is coordination. Oliver and Sophie dig into Oussama Abid's measurements of 1,782 agent PRs under a deterministic lease coordinator ('a rule an agent has to remember is not a rule'), Christopher Weir's ringleader thread running ~90 Claude Code workers, ShopBack's Slack-based domain agents and their safety lessons, a ReasonOS vendor post on putting rules in the build rather than the prompt, the AgentRun Show HN and its comment thread on agentic merge queues for Dependabot PRs, GitHub's portable agent skills and a Proof Agent verifier that never sees the coding agent's self-report, plus fleet control planes and two GitHub changelog items. Each story is mapped to Andrew's Cursor/GitHub/Azure factory, ending with one practical idea: make staging-failure alerts durable until acknowledged.

Sources discussed:

  • Agents under a coordinator: what broke, and how we caught it (Oussama Abid)
  • Coordinating coding agents in a large codebase (Christopher Weir)
  • Build the agent around where the work happens (Hoang Nguyen, ShopBack)
  • Agents write code fast. The hard part is knowing if it works. (Vamsi Pandari, ReasonOS - vendor post)
  • Show HN: AgentRun - open-source, Self-improving Managed Agents (Hacker News thread)
  • Introducing AgentRun: Run smarter agents. Use fewer tokens. (AgentRun blog - vendor post)
  • AgentRun on GitHub (Parcha-ai/agentrun)
  • Build once, run on any agent: A practical guide to agent skills (GitHub Blog, Andrea Griffiths)
  • GitHub Agentic Workflows blog - Agent of the Day (Daily A/B Testing Advisor)
  • Fleet Management for AI Coding Agents: Architecting the New DevOps Control Plane (Tamiz Uddin, DEV)
  • Actions for ARM32 Linux & Windows retirement (GitHub Changelog)
  • Secret scanning detects Cloudflare service tokens (GitHub Changelog)

item.title: Software Factory News - Thu 12 Nov 2026: Agents that built AWS Emulator, Harvey's harness, and CI built for agents
item.description:
Amazon's AWS Emulator built entirely by agents, Harvey's Spectre harness at 10,000 agent PRs, OpenAI's 1,000-hour Codex CI run, Robinhood's 60% no-review merges, CodeRabbit's 20x, making CI readable for agents, and two GitHub changes for Dependabot users.

Sources discussed:
